title: Winter NAO removal gave no clear reduction in England-Scotland rainfall correlation in 1951-2025
abstract: We tested whether a same-winter North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) adjustment reduces shared winter rainfall variation between England and Scotland. We used 75 complete winters from fixed Met Office and NOAA snapshots. For log rainfall, the correlation after removal of linear time was 0.520. After removal of time and mean winter NAO it was 0.618, with a 95% paired five-winter block interval of 0.454 to 0.746. The change was +0.098, with limits of -0.051 to +0.286. Thus the test gave no clear reduction, and positive residual correlation remained. Raw rainfall, squared NAO, monthly terms and period checks gave the same distinction. Covariance fell while fitted correlation rose because variance removal differed between countries. This does not identify a cause or measure joint water shortages. Country averages, one index, revised sources, 75 winters and block assumptions limit inference. New code, aggregate evidence, exact source hashes, a figure and numerical checks are included. External records remain outside the signed package.

display.caption: England-Scotland winter rainfall correlations after time and NAO adjustment, and paired changes with 95% block intervals. Positive residual correlation remains; all change intervals include zero.
